NEUTRAL_OBSERVATIONS.whatTheyAre: byte-level or set-membership comparisons whose answers are not in dispute: is the declared span inside a preregistered acceptable region; is the affectedDecision the preregistered one, a listed alternative, or neither; which unacceptable neighbour shares most vocabulary; does each preregistered conjunct appear in the declaration
NEUTRAL_OBSERVATIONS.whatTheyAreNot: verdicts. 'The span is not inside any acceptable region' is a fact; 'therefore D is INCORRECT' is a verdict, and no observation draws that line.
twoWeaknessesDisclosed: the neighbour-vocabulary metric is NOISY. On SF-01 it reports 60% overlap with 'whether a chuck guard is FITTED' although the declaration is about SECUREMENT of a specific mounting point — a different property. High overlap is not evidence of substitution and low overlap is not a defence. It is labelled A WEAK POINTER in the worksheet and was reworded after the first build for exactly this reason.

a no-gap row has no expected fact to compare against, so SF-04's observations degrade to nothing useful. Replaced with a comparison against that row's establishedByTheText and notEstablishedByTheText, which is the comparison that actually bears on it.
NEUTRAL_OBSERVATIONS.canBeRightAndStillMisleading: the §199 truth manifest is AI-authored and unreviewed, so a divergence from it is equally consistent with a defective declaration and a defective expectation. TRUTH_SPECIFICATION_DEFECT is a first-class outcome on every row, fact and refused declaration.

againstTheOwnerPreference.preference: prefer reducing structural coupling and provider-visible grammar complexity over merely shaving syntax to fit beneath the current limit
againstTheOwnerPreference.A_shortenDescriptions: contradicts it — shave-to-fit, risks the ten working rows, descriptions are load-bearing treatment (§104/§105/§138 each measured behaviour changing with description wording)
againstTheOwnerPreference.B_dropTheEnum: does not reduce coupling, but leaves the working path untouched and costs nothing the product depends on; the boundary already refuses unsupplied ids by exact set membership
againstTheOwnerPreference.C_separateStage: THE ONLY OPTION THAT REDUCES COUPLING. Leaves the first pass literally unchanged including its hash; removes the near-limit monolith; resolves the §199 tension where the model is shown a sourceId but a redacted text. Cost: a new protocol, preregistration and hosted validation, and a non-atomic analysis.
againstTheOwnerPreference.D_dropStrictMode: solves the stated problem and creates a larger one; §104 and §105 measured what strict-mode schema constraints are doing. Recorded for completeness, not put forward as serious.

twoThingsNotLeftUnsaid: C's cost is a whole validation cycle, and §195/§197/§198/§199 have already passed without a semantic result. B exercises the governed arm far sooner and is NOT a commitment against C.

neither B nor C is PROVEN to fit — the threshold is undocumented. Any option should be validated by an offline request build followed by a SINGLE-ROW TRANSPORT CANARY, the §199 pattern that worked and cost one call.

CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.observed: SG-01 at position 3 and SG-02 at position 8 shared an identical normalised signature with four completed inferences between them. The two-consecutive rule correctly did not trip. The rule worked as specified; the specification is what is in question.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.costOfTheGap: $0.00 in money — neither reached inference — but ONE COHORT ROW was spent rediscovering what the first had established. Cohort rows are the real currency.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.recommendation: KEEP adjacency AND ADD a stage-local signature memory, gated on a DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACT_REJECTION classification. Stop when either (a) two consecutive attempts share a signature, or (b) a signature has already occurred for the same stage + request-contract class + wire-schema class AND the rejection is contract-deterministic.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.whyBothAreNeeded: adjacency is the right guard against STOCHASTIC model failure and the wrong guard against a CAPABILITY-CLASS failure, whose incidence is determined by row class rather than by chance. Both are true at once.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.classificationMustBeConservative: unknown ⇒ TRANSIENT. Misclassifying a transient failure as deterministic truncates a run over a blip and destroys behavioural evidence; the opposite error only wastes a row at $0.00.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.riskStated: clause (b) can stop a run on a SINGLE observation. If a grammar-size rejection were ever non-deterministic, (b) would halt a cohort a retry would have completed. Mitigation: the run stops, records the signature, preserves everything obtained, and a successor re-authorization re-issues.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOMMENDATION.whatItWouldNotHaveChanged: SG-02 would still be unexercised and S/N/O/T would still be NOT_EXERCISED. The recommendation saves a ROW, not a RESULT.
